key_insight: Machine learning can identify degradation mechanisms in simulated lead-free RbSn₀.₅Ge₀.₅I₃ solar cells, but its reliability depends on training coverage and sampling design.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support post-fabrication diagnosis from electrical measurements, while replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raises simulated efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly through fill-factor improvement.
method: Compare forward-performance surrogates trained on factorial-grid and Latin-hypercube samples.
Use temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit voltage to classify six potentially co-occurring degradation mechanisms.
evidence_signal: The diagnostic classifier achieves macro F₁ = 0.938 versus 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline; grid-trained XGBoost drops from R² = 0.9997 on held-out grid points to 0.58 on independently sampled devices, while Latin-hypercube training achieves 0.995.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based, and the diagnostic classifier does not generalize to mechanism combinations absent from training.
paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
